title: Counting and 'the': -taa, -ti, -jon, -khaanaa
description: Use the classifier endings to say 'the', to count things and people, and to talk about a little or a lot.

guide.title: -টা: 'the', and the counting ending
guide.text:
The ending -টা (-taa) has two jobs.

On a noun it means 'the': বই 'book' - বইটা 'the book'; চাবি 'key' - চাবিটা 'the key'. Use it when both of you know which one is meant.

On a number it lets you count things: একটা বই 'one book, a book', পাঁচটা বই 'five books'. A number cannot normally stand directly before a noun without it. The noun stays singular.

Kolkata speech has three irregular forms: দুটো (duto), তিনটে (tinte), চারটে (chaarte). Everything else is regular: একটা, পাঁচটা, ছটা, সাতটা, আটটা, নটা, দশটা. Bangladesh standard uses -টা throughout: দুইটা, তিনটা, চারটা.

It also attaches to other counting words: কটা (kotaa) 'how many?', কয়েকটা (koyektaa) 'a few', অনেকগুলো 'many'.

guide.title: Number before or after the noun
guide.text:
Where you put the counted number changes the meaning.

Number + classifier BEFORE the noun is indefinite: দুটো বই - 'two books' (any two).

Noun first, then number + classifier, is definite: বই দুটো - 'the two books'.

In the same way একটা বই is 'a book', and বইটা is 'the book'.

guide.title: -টি, -জন, -খানা
guide.text:
-টি (-ti) is a gentler version of -টা. It suggests that the thing is small, dear or being spoken of politely, and it is the normal form in writing: একটি ছেলে 'a boy', ছেলেটি 'the boy', মেয়েটি 'the girl'. In speech -টা about a person can sound offhand; -টি never does.

-জন (-jon) counts people: একজন (ekjon), দুজন (dujon), তিনজন, কজন? It goes on the number only, never on the noun: একজন লোক 'a man', দুজন ছাত্র 'two students'. People can also be counted with -টা or -টি when they are children or when you are being casual: দুটো ছেলে.

-খানা (-khaanaa) is used for solid, flat or made objects - books, letters, saris, plates, houses, rooms: একখানা শাড়ি 'a sari', বইখানা 'the book'. It is optional (-টা is always possible) but you will hear it often in West Bengal. A lighter form is -খানি.

guide.title: Plural, and 'a little'
guide.text:
-গুলো (-gulo) is the plural of -টা: 'the ...s'. বইগুলো 'the books', এগুলো 'these'. The politer and written form is -গুলি (-guli). It is only used when the plural is definite and no number is given; after a number the noun stays bare.

For people, the plural ending is -রা (-raa): ছেলেরা 'the boys', বাচ্চারা 'the children'.

-টুকু (-tuku) means 'the little bit of': জলটুকু 'that little bit of water', এইটুকু 'just this much'.

একটু (ektu) is 'a little' of something you cannot count, and by extension the word that softens every request: একটু চিনি 'a little sugar', একটু দাঁড়ান 'wait a little'. Do not confuse it with একটা, 'one (thing)'.

examples.english: Put the books on the table.
Drink up that little bit of water.

phrases.note: For family members the verb আছে is often left out.
-ti is the polite, affectionate form of -taa.
The respectful verb ending is used for an adult stranger.

phrases.english: Put the books on the table.

phrases.note: একটু for things you cannot count.

phrases.english: Drink up that little bit of water.
